title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-08-05
content:
Weekly Serving Runtime Update — kernel / KV cache / batching
Date: 2026-08-05
Owner: Avery Patel
Summary: Focus this week on stabilizing the new fused attention kernel, finishing the KV cache eviction refactor, and iterating on batching heuristics for mixed short/long workloads. We landed two perf PRs (see links) and saw good improvements on 8k-context tails, but there's a regression under heavy simultaneous small-request load that needs follow-up.

Highlights / Wins:
- Fused attention kernel v2 merged (PR #1342). Microbenchmarks show 18–24% p50 token latency improvement on A100 for 2k–8k contexts. Reduced peak GPU memory by ~6% due to reworked buffer layout.
- KV cache eviction refactor (PR #1337) rolled to staging. New LRU-with-segmentation policy reduces thrash on long-chat workloads; staging e2e tests show ~12% lower token compute for customer workload x2.
- Batching heuristic: added per-model dynamic batch sizing that lowers average latency for mixed request profiles. Enabled on dedicated clusters as an opt-in flag.

Known Issues / Regressions:
- Regression under high QPS with many concurrent 1–3 token requests: p95 latency increases ~40% in canary. Root cause likely greedy batching window interaction with the new fused kernel's scheduling.
- Memory leak observed in streaming path when clients disconnect mid-stream; leak seems correlated with in-flight KV segments not being cleaned up. Repro steps added to JIRA-INF-7821.

Metrics / Numbers (staging, week-over-week):
- p50 token latency (gpt-like-7b, 2k context): 18% down (improved)
- p95 latency (high-QPS small-requests): +40% (regression)
- GPU memory peak (8k workloads): -6%
- Token throughput per GPU (batched long sequences): +15%

Deployments / Rollouts:
- Fused kernel v2: deployed to staging pool A, scheduled canary on 3 dedicated clusters tomorrow (08-06). Rollback plan prepared.
- KV cache refactor: enabled on internal staging only; will enable opt-in for a subset of Dedicated customers next week.

Work in Progress / Next Week:
- Investigate batching window + fused kernel scheduling interaction. Plan: reproduce with smaller test harness, add instrumentation to the scheduler (owner: Jordan).
- Fix streaming disconnect leak: add defensive cleanup for KV segments and add unit tests covering mid-stream disconnects (owner: Samira).
- Tune dynamic batch sizing thresholds and collect real-customer traces to set defaults (owner: Diego).
- Run full regression suite on canary clusters with synthetic high-QPS small-request workload.

Action Items / Owners:
- Jordan Lee: scheduler instrumentation + reproduce p95 regression (target: 08-07).
- Samira Khan: streaming disconnect memory leak patch + tests (target: 08-06).
- Diego Martinez: telemetry capture for dynamic batching and proposal for safe defaults (target: 08-10).
- Avery Patel: coordinate canary rollout and rollback triggers; update runbook.

Notes / Discussion Points:
- Consider temporary throttling / backpressure for very short requests until scheduler fix in place; this is low-friction and could mitigate customer impact.
- Evaluate whether fused kernel should expose a scheduling hint API so the runtime can prefer smaller or larger batch groupings depending on request mix.
- We should add a targeted chaos test that simulates client disconnects during streaming to prevent future leaks.

Attachments / Links:
- PR #1342: fused attention kernel v2 — https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1342
- PR #1337: KV cache eviction refactor — https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1337
- JIRA-INF-7821: streaming disconnect leak reproduction and triage

Quick Notes to self:
- Keep communication tight with SRE during canary; set a lower p95 threshold for auto-rollback.
- Collect a couple of real request traces from a high-QPS customer for batching tuning (ask CS for opt-in).

End of update.
